Definition: probably to be heavy, i.e. (figuratively) honorable
BiblicalUsage: The princes of the earth take counsel together against the LORD and His anointed, and Deborah's song calls the kings to hear what God has done. Wisdom speaks for herself: by me princes rule, and nobles decree justice. Yet the same word bows before a greater power, for God brings the princes to nothing and makes the judges of the earth as vanity.
TheologicalSignificance: I am convinced that no ruler stands above the God who raised him up. Princes rule only because Wisdom lends them her authority, and the moment they turn that authority against the LORD, He brings them to nothing. That is why I do not put my hope in princes, however strong they look.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
